title: Supporting Check: Is the commitment_indices mapping bijective on equivalence classes?
state_context: VerifyCellKZGProofBatch delegates to ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch. In the EIP-7594 / PeerDAS KZG scheme, each cell in the extended polynomial domain has a cell_index (0..CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB-1), which equals the column_index (0..NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS-1). One data column sidecar contains one cell per blob at a single column position. So sidecar.Index is the correct cell_index for all cells within that sidecar.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs constructs flat arrays of (commitment, cellIndex, cell, proof) tuples from sidecars. For each sidecar, sidecar.Index is the column index (0..127), used as cellIndices for VerifyCellKZGProofBatch. There is no deduplication of commitments — all commitment bytes from all sidecars are passed directly. The question of bijectivity applies at the cryptographic commitment level: the KZG batch verifier uses a random linear combination internally (see c-kzg-4844 implementation), so no explicit commitment_indices mapping in Go code exists that could be bijective or non-bijective. The mapping is implicit in the (commitment, cellIndex) pairing.
state_anomalies_found: No Go-level commitment deduplication exists — commitments are passed one-to-one with cells
sidecar.Index (column index 0-127) is correctly used as the KZG cell index in the batch API
For multiple blobs in one sidecar, KzgCommitments[i] maps to Column[i] at the same sidecar.Index — a 1:1 mapping within the sidecar
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: No caching in the commitment mapping path. Direct pass-through to ckzg4844 library.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs is stateless — no shared state between calls.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: The commitment_indices mapping is: each tuple (commitment_i, cell_index_i) = (sidecar.KzgCommitments[blobIdx], sidecar.Index). Within one sidecar, this is bijective because there is exactly one cell per blob per column, and sidecar.Index identifies the column. Across sidecars in the same batch, different sidecars may share the same commitment bytes (if the same blob appears in multiple columns), but the cell_indices differ — the batch verifier handles this correctly. No aliasing vulnerability exists.
attack_scenarios: Attacker sends duplicate sidecar.Index values: VerifyDataColumnSidecar checks sidecar.Index < numberOfColumns but does not prevent duplicates in the same batch. However, validateWithKzgBatchVerifier is called with a slice of one sidecar at a time (roDataColumns := []blocks.RODataColumn{roDataColumn}), so cross-sidecar aliasing within a single validation call is impossible.

If the batch verifier (kzgVerifierRoutine) groups two sidecars with the same column index from different block roots: VerifyCellKZGProofBatch would receive the same cellIndex twice with potentially different commitments, leading to a single verification result that applies to both — but this would result in rejection rather than acceptance of invalid proofs, since the linear combination would fail.
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: None identified for the bijection property.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The commitment mapping is exercised on every P2P gossip data column sidecar that passes pre-filters. The mapping path is: validateDataColumn -> validateWithKzgBatchVerifier -> kzgVerifierRoutine -> verifyKzgBatch -> VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs -> VerifyCellKZGProofBatch.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: Attacker can control KzgCommitments, Column, KzgProofs, and Index fields within structural bounds.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant 'commitment_i maps uniquely to equivalence class_i' holds because: (1) within a single validateDataColumn call, exactly one sidecar is processed; (2) the (commitment, cellIndex) tuples are correctly aligned by construction (i-th commitment, i-th cell, sidecar.Index); (3) the ckzg4844 KZG batch verifier uses random scalars for linear combination, providing security regardless of repeated commitment values. No bijection violation is possible through the Go code.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs constructs aligned (commitment, cellIndex, cell, proof) arrays
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient. The 1:1 alignment of commitment-to-cell is enforced by array indexing. No off-by-one or aliasing is possible in the construction loop.
edge_cases: Multiple blobs per sidecar: commitment[i] corresponds to column[i] at column index sidecar.Index — correct
Empty sidecar.Column: VerifyDataColumnSidecar rejects len(KzgCommitments)==0 before reaching KZG verification

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: No bijection violation exists. The commitment_indices mapping is a direct 1:1 array alignment, not a deduplication map. The sidecar.Index (column index) is the correct KZG cell index parameter. The ckzg4844 batch verifier is cryptographically sound regardless of repeated commitment values.

title: Supporting Check: Can a malicious P2P peer exploit commitment deduplication to forge valid proofs?
state_context: kzgChan is a buffered channel (capacity checked in service initialization). kzgVerifierRoutine drains all available items non-blockingly after receiving the first item. Any item failing batch verification triggers an individual fallback, correctly rejecting the invalid sidecar. However, the cross-contamination causes ALL legitimate sidecars in the same batch to also undergo individual verification — amplifying CPU cost per attacker message.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The batch KZG verifier groups items from multiple concurrent validateDataColumn calls into a single VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs invocation. The result (error or nil) is shared across ALL items in the batch. If one item has an invalid KZG proof but passes all pre-filters (subnet, slot, inclusion proof, proposer signature), the entire batch result is an error. All items then fall through to individual re-verification via validateUnbatchedColumnsKzg. The legitimate items CORRECTLY pass their individual verification and are accepted. The invalid item CORRECTLY fails and is rejected. However, the CPU cost of individual verification is O(cells_per_sidecar) per sidecar, so a batch of N sidecars costs O(N * cells) instead of O(N + cells) when contaminated.
state_anomalies_found: Cross-contamination: a single invalid sidecar causes ALL sidecars in the same batch to undergo individual re-verification
Amplification factor: attacker sends 1 invalid sidecar per slot, causing O(concurrent_valid_sidecars) additional verifications
Channel backpressure: if kzgChan fills (capacity depends on service init), validateWithKzgBatchVerifier blocks for up to SecondsPerSlot (12s) before returning ValidationIgnore for legitimate sidecars
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: No caching in the verification path. Each sidecar's KZG proof is verified from scratch.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: kzgVerifierRoutine is a single goroutine processing the channel. Cross-contamination is inherent to the batch design. No race condition — the single goroutine processes one batch at a time.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: CONCRETE ATTACK PATH: (1) Attacker crafts a structurally valid data column sidecar: correct subnet, valid slot range, valid inclusion proof (for a real block), valid proposer signature — but with an INVALID KZG cell proof (random bytes in KzgProofs). (2) Attacker broadcasts at a rate of ~10-20 per second to populate the kzgChan with cross-contaminating items. (3) Each attacker sidecar injected into a batch causes ALL legitimate sidecars in that batch to undergo individual re-verification. (4) Under sufficient flood (filling kzgChan), legitimate sidecars experience slot-timeout (12s) delays and are returned as ValidationIgnore — effectively dropped. (5) The node fails to process legitimate data column sidecars, causing data availability gaps.

counterexample.description: An attacker sends structurally valid sidecars with invalid KZG proofs at a high rate. These pass all pre-filters before KZG verification (subnet, slot, inclusion proof, proposer signature). In the batch verifier, these contaminate batches with legitimate sidecars, triggering O(batch_size) individual re-verifications and potentially exhausting the kzgChan buffer, causing legitimate sidecar ValidationIgnore timeouts.
counterexample.preconditions: Attacker knows a valid block root, can craft valid inclusion proofs, has a valid proposer signature (or uses a separate valid sidecar body with a modified KzgProofs field).
counterexample.impact: Liveness violation: legitimate data column sidecars are dropped (ValidationIgnore) during the flood. Repeated across slots → node falls behind on data availability.

attack_scenarios: Batch contamination DoS: attacker floods kzgChan with near-valid sidecars (all checks pass except KZG proof), causing batch failures and O(batch_size) individual re-verification CPU cost
Channel exhaustion: attacker sustains high-rate flood to keep kzgChan near-full, causing 12s timeouts on legitimate sidecars
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: Attack is most effective when kzgChan is under high load (many legitimate sidecars arriving simultaneously). Slot boundaries are natural high-load periods.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The attack path requires only P2P gossip access. The attacker must construct sidecars that pass: (1) decodePubsubMessage, (2) ValidFields (structural), (3) CorrectSubnet, (4) NotFromFutureSlot, (5) SlotAboveFinalized, (6) SidecarParentSeen, (7) SidecarParentValid, (8) ValidProposerSignature, (9) SidecarParentSlotLower, (10) SidecarDescendsFromFinalized, (11) SidecarInclusionProven. Steps 8 and 11 are the hardest — requiring valid proposer signatures and valid inclusion proofs. These can be obtained by monitoring the network and replaying valid sidecar headers with modified KzgProofs.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: Attacker with network access can observe valid sidecar headers and inject modified versions with invalid KZG proofs.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The security invariant 'only sidecars with valid KZG proofs are accepted' HOLDS — the fallback correctly rejects invalid sidecars. However, the performance invariant 'invalid sidecars are isolated and do not affect processing of legitimate sidecars' is VIOLATED by the cross-contamination design. The batch verifier trades isolation for efficiency.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Correctness guard is sufficient. Performance/isolation guard is insufficient — invalid items in a batch cause ALL items in the batch to fall back to individual verification.
edge_cases: kzgChan timeout: if kzgVerifierRoutine is overloaded, validateWithKzgBatchVerifier times out and returns ValidationIgnore — legitimate sidecars are silently dropped
Single-item batches: when kzgChan is low-traffic, each sidecar is verified alone — no cross-contamination, but no benefit of batching either

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: A P2P attacker can craft structurally valid sidecars (passing all pre-filters including proposer signature and inclusion proof) with invalid KZG proofs. These contaminate batch KZG verification groups, causing O(batch_size) re-verifications per attacker message and potential channel exhaustion leading to legitimate sidecar drops (ValidationIgnore). This is a liveness vulnerability: the node may drop valid data column sidecars under sustained attack, potentially causing data availability failures.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Redesign verifyKzgBatch to isolate verification failures: use individual verification for each item rather than a single batch call, OR implement per-verifier result tracking so batch failures only affect the failing item. Alternatively, add rate-limiting of KZG-failed sidecars per peer, and use the fallback result to individually report the per-item outcome rather than broadcasting the batch failure.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.severity_estimate: Medium — liveness impact, requires constructing near-valid sidecars (non-trivial but feasible for an attacker with network access)

title: Supporting Check: What is the impact on validator-node if commitment deduplication fails?
state_context: Data column sidecars are required for data availability sampling in PeerDAS. If a node fails to receive and process sufficient data column sidecars for a block, it cannot confirm data availability. Validators use data availability for fork choice and attestation decisions. A node that systematically drops valid sidecars may make incorrect fork choice decisions, potentially causing it to attest to unavailable blocks or to refuse to attest to available ones — both are consensus-level issues.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The impact pathway is: (1) kzgChan timeout causes ValidationIgnore for valid sidecars -> (2) msg.ValidatorData not set, DataColumnReceived event not fired -> (3) sidecar not stored in dataColumnStorage -> (4) node's view of block data availability is incomplete -> (5) if node custodies N columns and receives < N due to drops, it cannot confirm data availability for that block -> (6) fork choice and attestation decisions may be affected. The blast radius depends on how many sidecars are dropped and whether the node can recover them via sampling or reconstruction.
state_anomalies_found: Dropped sidecars are not queued for retry — ValidationIgnore is final for that gossip message delivery
Reconstruction path (reconstructSaveBroadcastDataColumnSidecars) is triggered separately and may recover some drops if enough columns are stored by other means
If all custody columns for a block are dropped, the node cannot reconstruct and will mark the block as data-unavailable
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: seenDataColumnCache uses slot/proposerIndex/columnIndex as key. If a sidecar is dropped (ValidationIgnore), the key is not set in the seen cache. If the same sidecar arrives again via another peer, it can be processed — partial recovery possible.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: Concurrent sidecar arrivals for the same column index from different peers: the second arrival may succeed if the first was dropped. However, under sustained DoS, both may be in the contaminated batch.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: IMPACT CHAIN: Attacker sustains KZG batch contamination flood for multiple consecutive slots. For each slot, legitimate data column sidecars for custody columns arrive but are ValidationIgnored due to kzgChan timeout. The reconstruction path (reconstructSaveBroadcastDataColumnSidecars) checks storedColumnsCount >= MinimumColumnCountToReconstruct() but since storage is empty (no sidecars stored), reconstruction cannot proceed. The node's dataColumnStorage remains empty for that block root. The node cannot confirm data availability. If the node is a validator, it may issue an attestation without data availability confirmation — a consensus-level liveness violation.

counterexample.description: Under sustained kzgChan saturation attack (from CHK-0127), a validator node's custody columns are all dropped. The reconstruction path has no stored columns and cannot recover. The node proceeds to fork choice without data availability confirmation for that block — potential liveness or safety violation depending on the client's data availability implementation.
counterexample.preconditions: Attack from CHK-0127 sustained across full slot duration (12s). Node cannot receive sidecars from alternative sources during attack.
counterexample.impact: Validator node may attest to blocks without confirmed data availability, or may fail to attest due to data availability uncertainty — both are consensus-layer concerns.

attack_scenarios: Sustained kzgChan saturation across a slot: all custody columns dropped → data availability not confirmable → attestation quality degraded
Targeted attack against validator nodes: selectively attack nodes during their attestation duty slot to prevent correct attestation
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: Attack must be sustained through the entire slot window (12s) to prevent any legitimate sidecar from being processed.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The downstream consensus impact is contingent on the CHK-0127 liveness vulnerability being exploited. The impact pathway requires: (1) sustained kzgChan saturation, (2) no alternative delivery path for sidecars (no req/resp fallback during attack), (3) no peer penalization for near-valid invalid sidecars fast enough to block the attack.
entry_points: P2P gossip /data_column_sidecar_N/ topic (via CHK-0127 attack vector)
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: Inherits from CHK-0127. Additional impact from consensus-layer data availability decisions.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant 'validator nodes always have confirmed data availability before attestation if data is available on the network' is conditionally violated when the kzgChan saturation attack from CHK-0127 is active. The reconstruction path provides a partial recovery mechanism but requires storedColumnsCount >= 64, which is impossible if all incoming sidecars are dropped. Secondary delivery paths (req/resp) may mitigate if not also overwhelmed.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Reconstruction path in reconstructSaveBroadcastDataColumnSidecars as secondary recovery
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Insufficient under sustained attack — reconstruction requires pre-stored columns that are unavailable if all gossip is dropped.
edge_cases: If only some custody columns are dropped: reconstruction may succeed if >= 64 unique columns are stored from other sidecars
Attestation delay: some clients may delay attestation waiting for data availability — this could reduce but not eliminate the consensus impact

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The downstream consensus impact of the CHK-0127 batch verifier cross-contamination vulnerability includes data availability confirmation failures for validator nodes. A validator node subject to kzgChan saturation attack may fail to confirm data availability for blocks during attacked slots, potentially issuing attestations without data availability guarantees — a consensus safety/liveness concern in the PeerDAS data availability sampling protocol.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Fix CHK-0127 (batch verifier isolation) to mitigate this downstream impact. Additionally, implement an explicit req/resp fallback path for sidecars that were not received via gossip during attack conditions.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.severity_estimate: Medium — conditional on CHK-0127 being exploited; consensus-layer liveness impact

title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Does recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs reject input with fewer than 50% cells?
state_context: DataColumnStorageSummary uses a boolean mask indexed by column index (0..NumberOfColumns-1). Count() iterates the mask and returns the number of true entries. Each column index can only be marked true once — structural deduplication at the storage level. This is consistent with the map-based deduplication in ReconstructDataColumnSidecars.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The 50% threshold is enforced at two layers: (1) the storage layer via DataColumnStorageSummary boolean mask Count() in reconstructSaveBroadcastDataColumnSidecars, and (2) the reconstruction layer via the sidecarByIndex map length check in ReconstructDataColumnSidecars. Both layers deduplicate by column index, ensuring the threshold operates on unique column counts. For N=128 columns, MinimumColumnCountToReconstruct() = (128+1)/2 = 64 = 128/2. The RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs (ckzg4844) function is only called when at least 64 unique cells are available.
state_anomalies_found: Last-write-wins for duplicate column indices in sidecarByIndex map — acceptable since all sidecars with the same column index should have identical cell data (same block root is verified)

No upper bound check on sidecarCount — if NumberOfColumns somehow reported as 1 via config, MinimumColumnCountToReconstruct() = 1, and only 1 unique column would be required. Not a realistic attack vector.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: DataColumnStorageSummary.Count() is based on a boolean mask — deduplication is structurally enforced. No inflation of stored count is possible.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: reconstructSaveBroadcastDataColumnSidecars acquires reconstructionLock before checking storedColumnsCount, preventing concurrent threshold checks.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No counterexample found. The threshold enforcement is correct and sufficient. Duplicate sidecars with the same column index cannot inflate the unique count at either the storage or reconstruction layer. The ckzg4844.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs function is only called with >= 64 unique column indices.
attack_scenarios: Attacker provides 64+ sidecars all with same column index: sidecarByIndex has 1 entry, threshold check fails (1 < 64), returns ErrNotEnoughDataColumnSidecars. No cryptographic operation occurs.
Attacker provides exactly 63 unique sidecars: 63 < 64, threshold check fails. Correct.
Attacker provides exactly 64 unique sidecars: 64 < 64 = false, reconstruction proceeds. Correct boundary behavior.
Attacker provides 0 sidecars: len(verifiedRoSidecars)==0 check triggers first. Correct.
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: reconstructionLock prevents race conditions at the threshold check.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: ReconstructDataColumnSidecars is not directly callable from P2P. It is invoked only from reconstructSaveBroadcastDataColumnSidecars (internal) which operates on already KZG-verified stored sidecars. An attacker cannot pass attacker-controlled unverified cells to RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs through this path.
entry_points: Internal reconstruction triggered by block/sidecar arrival events, not directly from P2P
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: No direct P2P path to call ReconstructDataColumnSidecars with attacker-controlled data. All input sidecars must be KZG-verified before storage.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant 'RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs is always called with >= N/2 unique cell indices' holds. Proof: (1) sidecarByIndex deduplicates by column index; (2) threshold check on len(sidecarByIndex) ensures >= 64 unique columns; (3) cellsIndices are derived directly from sidecarByIndex keys, so they are unique; (4) RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs is only called if this check passes.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: uint64(sidecarCount) < MinimumColumnCountToReconstruct() check on deduplicated sidecarByIndex
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient. Both deduplication and threshold are correctly implemented.
edge_cases: Exactly 64 unique columns: reconstructs correctly (64 = threshold boundary, passes check)
All 128 columns: stored count == numberOfColumns triggers early return in caller — reconstruction not needed

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The 50% threshold is correctly enforced at both the storage layer and the reconstruction layer. Deduplication by column index is consistent across both layers. RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs is never called with fewer than 64 unique cells via this code path. No bypass or off-by-one vulnerability exists.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: No fix required. Implementation is correct.

title: Supporting Check: Is the 50% threshold correctly derived from CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB constant?
state_context: Two different threshold derivations exist in the codebase: (1) MinimumColumnCountToReconstruct uses runtime params.BeaconConfig().NumberOfColumns; (2) ReconstructBlobs uses compile-time fieldparams.CellsPerBlob. For current config (NumberOfColumns=128, CellsPerBlob=64), both give 64. The relationship NumberOfColumns = 2 * CellsPerBlob is not enforced by code but is maintained by consistent config values.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: MinimumColumnCountToReconstruct = (params.BeaconConfig().NumberOfColumns + 1) / 2. For NumberOfColumns=128: (128+1)/2 = 64 (integer division). This equals fieldparams.CellsPerBlob=64 and equals CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB/2 = 128/2 = 64. The formula (N+1)/2 equals ceil(N/2): for even N, this equals N/2; for odd N, this equals (N+1)/2. The Reed-Solomon reconstruction threshold is N/2 cells for a systematic (N/2, N) code, or equivalently N/2 cells from any N positions in the extended domain. For N=128, threshold = 64. The formula is algebraically correct for even N=128.
state_anomalies_found: Threshold uses runtime config (params.BeaconConfig().NumberOfColumns) while CellsPerBlob threshold in ReconstructBlobs uses compile-time constant (fieldparams.CellsPerBlob)
No compile-time or startup assertion that params.BeaconConfig().NumberOfColumns == 2 * fieldparams.CellsPerBlob

If NumberOfColumns were misconfigured (e.g., changed without updating CellsPerBlob), the two threshold functions would diverge — ReconstructDataColumnSidecars and ReconstructBlobs would have different thresholds
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: MinimumColumnCountToReconstruct reads global config per call — no caching, no staleness risk, but also no compile-time enforcement.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: params.BeaconConfig() is a read-only global after initialization. No concurrent modification concern.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: For the current configuration (NumberOfColumns=128, CellsPerBlob=64): MinimumColumnCountToReconstruct() = 64 = fieldparams.CellsPerBlob. Both thresholds are identical. No off-by-one, no integer overflow (uint64 arithmetic with small values). The formula is correct. The config source discrepancy is a maintenance concern but not a current vulnerability.
attack_scenarios: If an operator misconfigures NumberOfColumns (e.g., sets to 256): MinimumColumnCountToReconstruct() = 128 but fieldparams.CellsPerBlob = 64 — the ckzg4844 library would be called with 128 cells for a 128-column extended polynomial (correct threshold for the new config) — but ReconstructBlobs would still require only 64 columns. This is a misconfig scenario, not a P2P attack.
Integer overflow: NumberOfColumns = MaxUint64: (MaxUint64 + 1) / 2 = 0 due to overflow — any count would pass. Not possible in production config.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The threshold calculation is exercised only during internal reconstruction, not directly from P2P. No P2P attacker can manipulate params.BeaconConfig().NumberOfColumns.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: No P2P attack surface for threshold manipulation.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant 'MinimumColumnCountToReconstruct() equals the mathematical Reed-Solomon reconstruction threshold for the configured number of columns' holds for the current and intended configuration (NumberOfColumns=128, threshold=64). The formula (N+1)/2 is algebraically equivalent to ceil(N/2) which equals N/2 for even N. The Reed-Solomon threshold for a rate-1/2 code over N extended positions is exactly N/2.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Mathematically sufficient for the current configuration. A startup assertion would improve robustness.
edge_cases: NumberOfColumns = 0: threshold = (0+1)/2 = 0 — any count passes. Not a realistic config.
NumberOfColumns = 1: threshold = (1+1)/2 = 1 — only 1 column needed. Not valid for Reed-Solomon but not a realistic config.
NumberOfColumns != 2 * CellsPerBlob: ReconstructDataColumnSidecars and ReconstructBlobs would have different thresholds — maintenance bug, not current vulnerability

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The threshold (N+1)/2 = 64 is algebraically correct for N=128. No off-by-one, no integer overflow under realistic configurations, no P2P exploitability. The compile-time vs runtime source discrepancy between ReconstructDataColumnSidecars and ReconstructBlobs is a maintenance concern but not a security vulnerability — both produce the same value (64) for the current configuration.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Add a startup assertion: assert(params.BeaconConfig().NumberOfColumns == 2 * fieldparams.CellsPerBlob) to detect misconfigurations early. Consider unifying the threshold derivation to use a single source of truth.
